A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCAR research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v7 reports original fine-tuning experiments, stylometric analyses, component ablations, and fairness evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v8 retains these original empirical results and adds a sampling-time comparison in Appendix C.8.

M1.justification: The ranking objective, quality constraint, representation architecture, triplet regularization, and top-k selection procedure remain unchanged. CodeT5 is newly mentioned in Section 3 but was already documented in v7 Appendix A.1. Deduplication is recommended, not incorporated into SCAR.

E1.justification: The training sources, four programming languages, open-domain benchmarks, additional capability benchmarks, and bias-test populations are retained. The new timing study introduces no identified new dataset or task coverage. Anthropic RLHF is renamed HH-RLHF.

E2.justification: Random, Perplexity, Superfiltering, HFR, AlpaGasus, Diversity, and Longest remain the comparison algorithms in corresponding evaluations. The new timing table reuses these algorithms with additional GPT-2 configurations; those are experimental-setting additions.

E3.justification: Appendix C.8 introduces a timing protocol selecting 1,000 examples from 10,000, using an M4 Pro laptop or A100 40GB GPU and batch sizes of 16 or 2. It includes GPT-2-based Perplexity and Superfiltering configurations. Existing fine-tuning and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v8 adds a computational-efficiency analysis comparing selection costs in Appendix C.8. Appendix B.5 removes v7's informal report that preliminary cosine/Euclidean comparisons of RoBERTa embeddings revealed no meaningful patterns. Existing component ablations, independence analyses, bias evaluations, and response examples are retained.

E5.justification: Existing descriptive means and standard deviations are retained. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the new timing table introduces no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 16 reports selection times, including 1.8 minutes for SCAR and HFR, 1.5 minutes for GPT-2 Perplexity, and 1.5 hours for LLAMA3-8B Perplexity. Existing benchmark, ablation, stylometric, and bias-table values match. Section 4.2 removes the 90% filtering observation and revises the qualitative account of generator-source effects.

T1.justification: The method equations, conditional mutual-information formulas, and response-probability factorization are retained. Appendix B.5 adds the standard perplexity formula and explanatory discussion of existing concepts, without introducing new formal assumptions, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: identifying two response-style factors and selecting small, effective training subsets with SCAR. The 0.7–25% data-efficiency claims retain their scope; the revised wording does not establish a new core claim.

C2.justification: Appendix B.4 replaces asserted independence with a weaker interpretation of distinct, weakly correlated style dimensions. Appendix B.5 revises the rationale connecting semantic relatedness and surprisal. Section 4.2 distinguishes generator-source effects on human versus synthetic selection, and Limitations newly explains how duplicate instructions can reduce subset diversity.

D1.justification: v8 newly identifies guesslang and its access link for programming-language identification, documents hardware and batching for the timing study, and recommends deduplication before selection. Existing training hyperparameters, generation prompts, and SCAR code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v8 adds Liu et al. (2024), Salicchi et al. (2023), Sayeed et al. (2015), and Sung et al. (2018), while removing Le and Mikolov (2014) and Pennington et al. (2014). These changes refine the positioning of surprisal and relation-network modeling; Section 5's broader positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The title and affiliations change, terminology is standardized, and contributions, style factors, and baselines receive clearer list formatting. Appendix B.5 is substantially rewritten locally, and benchmark explanations are expanded. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v7's abbreviated response-example Table 22 moves to v8's main-text Table 1. The main stylometric/performance table is enlarged and receives a more descriptive caption, and a new timing table is added. Other tables reflow and renumber; all three figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: v8 improves practical assessability through the documented timing comparison and deduplication guidance, and Appendix B.4 interprets the unchanged evidence more cautiously. The enlarged main results table and earlier response example also improve accessibility. Some informal diagnostic detail is removed, and the timing evidence covers only one workload without uncertainty reporting, limiting the gains. Overall, these are useful refinements to an otherwise unchanged empirical study.
